title: Compute height of tree with deleted nodes; minimize deletions
description_html:
You are given a rooted tree (not necessarily binary) with n nodes labeled 1..n, described by parent-child edges, and a boolean array deleted[i] indicating whether node i is in a "deleted state".

When computing height you must skip deleted nodes:

  • A deleted node does not contribute to the height.
  • Its subtree still exists; traversing downward you may conceptually "pass through" deleted nodes to their children.

The tree height is the maximum length (in number of nodes) of a path from the root to any reachable non-deleted node after skipping deleted nodes. If no non-deleted node is reachable, the height is 0.

Part 1

Return the maximum height of the tree after skipping deleted nodes.

Part 2 (follow-up)

You may additionally mark more nodes deleted. After skipping deleted nodes, the resulting height must be at most K. Return the minimum number of additional deletions required.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 2·10^5
  • 1 ≤ K ≤ n

Example

Input
4 3
1 2
1 3
3 4
0 1 0 0
Output
3

Node 2 is deleted; the longest skip-deleted root path is 1 → 3 → 4 = 3 nodes.
